I don't have today's price move data for ConocoPhillips, so I can't tell you what direction the stock moved or by how much. However, the news flow around the stock has been shaped by two major themes this week: the company reported quarterly earnings on November 5th, and oil prices have come under pressure following Trump's comments suggesting the Iran conflict may be winding down soon.

Oil prices matter directly to ConocoPhillips' profitability—when crude falls, so typically does the company's near-term earnings power. Brent crude dropped below $90 a barrel after Trump's remarks on November 10th, a meaningful decline from the $107 per barrel Brent level in the current data. That said, US crude remains at nearly $100 per barrel, so the pressure is real but not severe. Without knowing which direction ConocoPhillips stock moved today, it's hard to say whether the market is focused on the earnings report itself or reacting to the oil price weakness from geopolitical optimism.
